docs.title: 8. Rendering with Jinja and LaTeX
docs.text:
LaTeX uses braces and percent signs everywhere, so the Jinja environment uses custom delimiters.

Purpose Delimiter Example Statement \BLOCK{ ... } \BLOCK{for e in events} Output \VAR{ ... } \VAR{run.status} Comment \#{ ... } removed from output Line statement %% %% if events Line comment %# removed from output

Limits that follow from this: no dict or set literals with braces inside \VAR{} or \BLOCK{}, because the first } closes the tag. Compute such values in Python. StrictUndefined is on, so a typo in a template fails the build loudly in tests rather than printing a blank in a bank report.

reports/scripts/render.py:

# LaTeX safe Jinja environment for the report templates.
from pathlib import Path

import jinja2

_TEX_MAP = {
    "\\": r"\textbackslash{}",
    "&": r"\&",
    "%": r"\%",
    "$": r"\$",
    "#": r"\#",
    "_": r"\_",
    "{": r"\{",
    "}": r"\}",
    "~": r"\textasciitilde{}",
    "^": r"\textasciicircum{}",
}


class RawTeX(str):
    pass


def tex_escape(value: object) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, RawTeX):
        return str(value)
    text = "" if value is None else str(value)
    return "".join(_TEX_MAP.get(ch, ch) for ch in text)


def ident(value: object) -> RawTeX:
    text = tex_escape(value)
    return RawTeX(
        text.replace(r"\_", r"\_\allowbreak{}").replace(".", r".\allowbreak{}")
    )


def breakable(value: object) -> RawTeX:
    parts = []
    for part in re.split(r"([^A-Za-z0-9\s])", "" if value is None else str(value)):
        if not part:
            continue
        parts.append(
            tex_escape(part)
            if part.isalnum() or part.isspace()
            else r"\allowbreak{}" + tex_escape(part)
        )
    return RawTeX("".join(parts))


def make_env(*template_dirs: Path) -> jinja2.Environment:
    env = jinja2.Environment(
        loader=jinja2.FileSystemLoader([str(p) for p in template_dirs]),
        block_start_string=r"\BLOCK{",
        block_end_string="}",
        variable_start_string=r"\VAR{",
        variable_end_string="}",
        comment_start_string=r"\#{",
        comment_end_string="}",
        line_statement_prefix="%%",
        line_comment_prefix="%#",
        trim_blocks=True,
        lstrip_blocks=True,
        autoescape=False,
        undefined=jinja2.StrictUndefined,
    )
    env.finalize = tex_escape
    env.filters.update({"raw": RawTeX, "ident": ident, "breakable": breakable})
    return env

finalize escapes every \VAR{} output automatically, so escaping is the default and opting out is explicit. Additional filters to implement and test: fmt_int (thin space thousands), fmt_pct, fmt_dur (1h 05m), fmt_ts (with zone label), state_colour, severity_colour, plural.

Template conventions:

  • One chapter per file, each starting with \section{...} and ending with a blank line.
  • Use partials for anything repeated twice: KPI card, event row, status pill, the "section unavailable" box.
  • Identifiers in tables use \texttt{\VAR{x | ident}} so long names such as raw.card_transactions break cleanly.
  • Free text in a table cell uses \VAR{x | breakable}, which allows a break at every punctuation mark. Without it a long message such as rows_landed=22500, cannot wrap and pushes the cell past the margin.
  • No logic that belongs in Python. Templates loop, branch on presence and format. Sorting, thresholds, joins and colour decisions are computed before rendering.
  • Free text from the warehouse is always plain \VAR{}. Only Python built values use raw.

Chapter excerpt (chapters/partials/event_table.tex.j2):

\BLOCK{if events}
\begin{longtable}{@{}p{2.4cm}p{3.6cm}p{9.6cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Severity} & \textbf{Where} & \textbf{What happened} \\
\midrule
\BLOCK{for e in events}
\severitytag{\VAR{e.severity | lower}} & \texttt{\VAR{e.subject | ident}} & \VAR{e.message} \\
\BLOCK{endfor}
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\BLOCK{else}
No events above INFO. All gates passed.
\BLOCK{endif}

docs.text:
main.tex is hand written and never generated. Python writes build/meta.tex and build/manifest.tex, so changing which chapters appear never touches the entry point.

$pdflatex = 'pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -no-shell-escape %O %S';

Compile command used everywhere (-jobname fixes the output name):

docs.title: 9. Design system
docs.text: All design tokens live in template/bankingreport.sty. Charts and TikZ read the same palette from reports/scripts/charts.py; keep both in step and test that they match.

docs.title: Colour
docs.text:
Layer colours are reused from docs/PIPELINE.md so a reader recognises them across docs, diagrams and the PDF. Layer colours mean a layer. Status colours mean a status. Never mix the two roles.

Role Name Stroke Fill Layer source #1D4ED8 #DBEAFE Layer orchestration #6D28D9 #EDE9FE Layer raw #C2410C #FFEDD5 Layer staging #0E7490 #CFFAFE Layer analytics #15803D #DCFCE7 Layer marts #BE185D #FCE7F3 Layer publish #A16207 #FEF9C3 Layer audit #475569 #F1F5F9 Status ok, SUCCESS #15803D #DCFCE7 Status warn, PARTIAL, MINOR #A16207 #FEF9C3 Status bad, FAILED, MAJOR #B91C1C #FEE2E2 Status critical #7F1D1D #FECACA Status idle, UNKNOWN, SKIPPED #475569 #F1F5F9

Rules: status is always printed as a word or glyph next to the colour, so the page works in greyscale and for colour blind readers. Text on a fill uses the dark stroke colour. No gradients, shadows or decorative images.

docs.title: Typography
Components (macros in the style file)
docs.text:
Macro Use \statusbanner{state}{label} full width verdict band on page one \kpicard{title}{value}{subtitle}{state} four across metric cards \severitytag{sev} coloured pill with the severity word \statuspill{state} table cell status with word and colour \callout[ok\|warn\|bad]{title}{text} boxed note, built on tcolorbox \sectionunavailable{name} visible box when a section failed to collect

Tables use booktabs and longtable: thin rules, no vertical lines, light slate zebra rows, numbers right aligned, header repeated across pages. Header carries the report kind and run id, footer carries Internal, the generation time with zone and Page x of y. Set PDF title, author, subject and keywords through hyperref, enable bookmarks and clickable cross references.

docs.title: Page one
docs.text: Order is fixed: verdict banner, four KPI cards (tables ok, rows landed, DQ checks passed, duration against trailing median), "What needs attention" (top five events by severity, each with one runbook pointer), then the compact flow strip. If the run is healthy the attention block says so in one sentence and the space goes to the flow and one chart.

docs.title: Charts
docs.text:
Charts are matplotlib figures saved as vector PDF into figures/, created at the final printed size so fonts stay at their real size (full width 6.7 in by about 2.6 in, half width 3.3 in). The same fonts are registered from fonts/, pdf.fonttype is 42 so text stays selectable, and the fallback family is DejaVu Sans.

# Shared matplotlib style for report figures.
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager


def apply_style(font_dir: Path) -> None:
    for path in sorted(font_dir.glob("*.ttf")):
        font_manager.fontManager.addfont(str(path))
    plt.rcParams.update(
        {
            "font.family": ["Inter", "DejaVu Sans"],
            "font.size": 8.5,
            "pdf.fonttype": 42,
            "axes.spines.top": False,
            "axes.spines.right": False,
            "axes.edgecolor": "#475569",
            "axes.grid": True,
            "grid.color": "#E2E8F0",
            "grid.linewidth": 0.6,
            "axes.axisbelow": True,
            "savefig.bbox": "tight",
        }
    )

Chart rules: no 3D, no pie or donut, bars start at zero, at most four colours per chart, direct labels instead of legends where possible, one message per chart with the title stating it, threshold and median drawn as thin dashed lines, anomalies annotated with the value and the rule id. If a chart has no data, render a small "no data" placeholder box rather than an empty axis, and never fail the build for a missing chart.

Figure file Type Shows Chapter task_timeline.pdf horizontal timeline start and end per task, layer colour, retries hatched, failures outlined 03 volumes_dumbbell.pdf dumbbell rows landed today against trailing median per table 04 layer_rows.pdf grouped bars rows touched per layer in this run against median 04 dq_heatmap.pdf matrix check by layer with PASS, WARN, FAIL word in each cell 05 freshness_bullet.pdf bullet chart table age against its window 06 error_categories.pdf horizontal bars errors by category, final attempt marked 07 trend_duration.pdf line with band run duration over the last N runs, status markers 08 trend_failures.pdf small multiples failures, retries and DQ fails per source 08 publish_reconcile.pdf paired bars source rows against published rows per mart, gap highlighted 04

publish_reconcile exists because of the known publish lookback gap (for example the mart_support_performance 193 row difference in docs/RUNBOOK.md): a gap like that should be visible in the report the day it appears.

docs.title: Pipeline flow diagram
docs.text:
The flow is a TikZ picture generated from the steps list, so node colours and badges follow the run. Node fill is the layer colour, node border and badge are the status colour, the label carries the step name and duration. Node ids are slugs made by flow.py (n01, n02, and so on) so they never need escaping. Coordinates come from a fixed grid in flow.py: three extract nodes stacked on the left, then the gated chain, then publish and finalize.

\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\footnotesize}]
\BLOCK{for node in flow.nodes}
\node[flowstep, \VAR{node.layer | raw}, \VAR{node.state | raw}] (\VAR{node.id | raw}) at (\VAR{node.x | raw}, \VAR{node.y | raw}) {\VAR{node.label}\\{\scriptsize\VAR{node.duration}}};
\BLOCK{endfor}
\BLOCK{for edge in flow.edges}
\draw[flowarrow] (\VAR{edge.src | raw}) -- (\VAR{edge.dst | raw});
\BLOCK{endfor}
\end{tikzpicture}

flowstep, the layer names (raw, staging, analytics, marts, publish, audit) and the state names (ok, warn, bad, idle) are TikZ styles defined in the style file. The node style is called flowstep and not step, because step is a PGF key that already means something else. Values passed with raw are validated by Python against an allow list before rendering.

docs.title: 10. The builder
docs.text:
uv run python -m reports.scripts.build --kind daily --dag-id banking_delta_daily --dag-run-id "<id>"
uv run python -m reports.scripts.build --kind incident --dag-run-id "<id>"
uv run python -m reports.scripts.build --kind weekly
uv run python -m reports.scripts.build --fixture reports/data/fixtures/major_dq_fail.json
Flag Meaning --kind daily\|incident\|weekly which chapter set to build --dag-id, --dag-run-id which run to report, defaults to the latest --fixture PATH skip the database and use a context file --all-fixtures build every tracked fixture, one report each --no-pdf stop after rendering .tex (hermetic, no TeX needed) --no-charts safe mode, no figures and no TikZ flow --out DIR output root, wins over REPORT_OUTPUT_DIR --strict treat any degraded section as an error, for tests

Steps, in order, with a total budget under 60 seconds in CI and under 2 minutes in Airflow:

  1. Collect and write data/context.json, validate against the schema. The same document is copied next to the PDF as runs/RUN_KEY/context.json.
  2. Evaluate rules, attach events and verdict, decide which kinds to build.
  3. Draw charts into figures/, skipping any that fail.
  4. Render build/meta.tex, build/manifest.tex and the chapters. A chapter that still holds a \VAR{ or \BLOCK{ tag fails the build with exit code 2.
  5. Compile with latexmk -jobname=report main.tex. The LaTeX state of the job is deleted first, so a broken .aux from an earlier run cannot break this one. On failure retry once with --no-charts (safe mode) and mark the report "degraded" on page one.
  6. Copy to output/runs/RUN_KEY/<pdf name> and output/<pdf name> (latest): report.pdf for the daily, incident.pdf, weekly.pdf. Write the redacted compile log to build/<jobname>.log (report.log, incident.log, weekly.log). Prune runs older than REPORT_RETENTION_DAYS.
  7. Print a one line JSON result (kind, verdict, pages, path, degraded).

Exit codes: 0 built, 2 render or schema error, 3 compile failed even in safe mode, 1 usage error. RUN_KEY is the run id reduced to [A-Za-z0-9_] by paths.py.

docs.title: DAG change
docs.text:
banking_delta_daily gets one new task between finalize_audit and send_pipeline_summary. It runs after finalize_audit because that task reaps orphaned RUNNING rows and rolls up the final status the report must show.

flowchart LR
    MT["marts_tests"] --> PB["publish"]
    PB --> FIN["finalize_audit<br/>all_done"]
    FIN --> BR["build_report<br/>all_done, retries=1, 15m"]
    BR --> SUM["send_pipeline_summary<br/>all_done, attaches PDF"]
    BR -.->|"not in the failure gate"| GATE["fail_if_any_failed"]

    classDef af fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#6d28d9,color:#4c1d95,stroke-width:2px
    classDef audit fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#475569,color:#1e293b,stroke-width:2px
    classDef rep fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#a16207,color:#713f12,stroke-width:2px
    classDef gate fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#7f1d1d,stroke-width:2px
    class MT,PB af
    class FIN,SUM audit
    class BR rep
    class GATE gate
Task Command Retries and timeout Notes build_report python -m reports.scripts.build --kind daily --dag-id ... --dag-run-id ... 1 and 15m trigger_rule=all_done; builds incident.pdf too when any event is MAJOR or higher

Use the same command builder module the other tasks use, so airflow/tests/test_commands.py keeps proving that no secrets and no unquoted ids reach a command line. Template ids with {{ dag.dag_id }} and {{ run_id }}. Skeleton:

# build_report task wiring for banking_delta_daily.
build_report = BashOperator(
    task_id="build_report",
    bash_command=report_command(kind="daily"),
    trigger_rule="all_done",
    retries=1,
    retry_delay=timedelta(minutes=2),
    execution_timeout=timedelta(minutes=15),
)
finalize_audit >> build_report >> send_pipeline_summary

Rules for the wiring:

  • build_report is not an upstream of fail_if_any_failed. A PDF problem must not make a green pipeline red. The mail says "report unavailable" instead.
  • send_pipeline_summary is all_done, so it still sends when build_report failed.
  • Find the files by the deterministic path output/runs/RUN_KEY/, not through XCom.
  • Mount a named volume report_output at the worker's report output directory. With one worker the files are local; with several workers the volume (or object storage) is required, because the mail task may run on a different host.
  • Update airflow/tests/test_dag_integrity.py: the task exists, trigger_rule is all_done, it sits after finalize_audit and before send_pipeline_summary, it is not linked to the failure gate, and the retries and timeout match.

docs.title: Mail
docs.text:
Extend the existing notify.py and summary.py, never add a second SMTP path.

  • notify gains an attachments list. Attach with EmailMessage.add_attachment using application/pdf, file name Banking-Delta_<kind>_<YYYYMMDD>_<VERDICT>.pdf.
  • Skip an attachment larger than REPORT_MAX_ATTACH_MB (default 10) and say so in the body.
  • The body shows the verdict, the top three events (names and counts only) and a line stating whether the report was degraded or missing.
  • A missing file is a warning in the body, never an exception.
  • Recipients default to ALERT_EMAIL_TO, with REPORT_EMAIL_TO as an optional override.
  • Add tests to test_notify_render.py: attachment present, wrong size skipped, no attachment path still sends, subject marker unchanged.

docs.title: Weekly DAG and watchdog
docs.text:
• banking_report_weekly: schedule 0 8 * * 1 Asia/Kolkata, catchup=False, max_active_runs=1, one task build_weekly_report then a mail task reusing the mail helper. Created paused like the others, un pause deliberately.
  • Phase 2: when banking_watchdog raises [MISSED], [STUCK] or [WATCHDOG-ERROR], it calls --kind incident and attaches the PDF. The watchdog stays silent when healthy and must keep working if report building fails.

docs.title: Image and compose
docs.text:
TeX Live is large (roughly 500 to 800 MB). Recommended option: install it in the Airflow worker image, so the task runs exactly what python main.py and make report run, with no Docker socket mounted into Airflow. Both Dockerfiles read the same package list.

# TeX toolchain for the report builder, shared package list.
COPY reports/apt-packages.txt /tmp/apt-packages.txt
USER root
RUN apt-get update \
    && xargs -a /tmp/apt-packages.txt apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* /tmp/apt-packages.txt
USER airflow

Also copy reports/ into the image and run uv sync --frozen --group reports. Never mount /var/run/docker.sock into an Airflow container for this feature. reports/apt-packages.txt starts with latexmk, texlive-xetex, texlive-latex-recommended, texlive-latex-extra, texlive-pictures, texlive-fonts-recommended and fontconfig; trim or extend it after the first clean compile. texlive-fonts-recommended provides Latin Modern, which the pdfLaTeX fallback needs for microtype; fonts-inter is the system copy of Inter for the XeLaTeX build, next to the bundled files in reports/fonts/.

reports/Dockerfile is the standalone builder: it installs the same package list, adds the report runtime (jinja2, jsonschema, pyyaml, matplotlib, psycopg2-binary, python-dotenv) and copies src/ and reports/ into /work. The entry point compiles every fixture, so docker run needs no arguments.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Add every variable to .env.example and airflow/.env.airflow.example (tests/smoke/test_env_contract.py enforces it). Read them only in src/utils/config.py.

Variable Default Meaning REPORT_ENABLED true master switch for the Airflow task REPORT_OUTPUT_DIR reports/output root for PDFs REPORT_TIMEZONE Asia/Kolkata zone label used in the document REPORT_RETENTION_DAYS 30 prune older run folders REPORT_MAX_ATTACH_MB 10 skip larger attachments REPORT_EMAIL_TO empty optional override of ALERT_EMAIL_TO REPORT_TREND_RUNS 14 runs shown in trend charts

docs.title: 12. Make and tasks.bat targets
docs.text:
tests/smoke/test_make_parity.py fails when a Makefile target is missing from tasks.bat or when ci picks up a non hermetic target, so add every target to both files.

Target What it does Tier Agent may run report-fixture render every fixture to .tex with --no-pdf, no TeX and no database hermetic, part of make ci yes report-pdf compile every fixture to PDF with a local TeX Live tex tier, not in ci yes, when TeX is installed report-tex run the tex tier: every fixture compiles, the log has no error and no overfull box, the page budget holds tex tier, not in ci yes, when TeX is installed report-docker build reports/Dockerfile and compile the fixtures inside it tex tier yes report build the daily report against the environment .env points at reads the warehouse ask first report-incident RUN=<id> build an incident report for a run reads the warehouse ask first report-weekly build the weekly digest reads the warehouse ask first report-clean remove reports/build, reports/output and the generated figures local yes

On Windows, avoid installing MiKTeX: use the container.

docker build -t banking-report -f reports/Dockerfile .
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}/reports/output:/work/reports/output" banking-report

The image carries the TeX toolchain and the report runtime, so docker run compiles every fixture with no extra flags. The build context is the repository root because the image also copies src/.

docs.title: 13. Tests
docs.text:
Mirror source paths: reports/scripts/render.py is tested in tests/unit/reports/test_render.py. Mark every test (unit, smoke, or the new tex marker registered in pyproject.toml), otherwise it silently never runs.

Test Guards against tex_escape handles all ten special characters, None, unicode broken compiles from error text escape neutralises \input{...}, \write18, \immediate in free text LaTeX injection through audit messages RawTeX is the only escape bypass, StrictUndefined raises on a missing key silent blanks, accidental raw output severity rules, one table driven test per rule R001 to R018 wrong or downgraded severity verdict is the maximum severity, UNKNOWN never renders as ok false green report latest attempt per table decides the table status a retry that succeeded reported as failed redaction applied to every free text field, 300 character cap secrets in mail or PDF context.json validates against the schema for every fixture contract drift chapter selection per kind and drop_when_empty wrong chapters appearing deterministic render: same context gives byte identical .tex flaky diffs palette in charts.py equals the colours in the style file design drift chart functions return a figure for empty data build failure on quiet days build --fixture X --no-pdf leaves no \VAR{ or \BLOCK{ in build/ unrendered template text tex tier: every fixture compiles, the log has no ! errors, pages within budget broken LaTeX tex tier: safe mode compiles when the figures directory is empty degraded path rot mail: attachment added, oversize skipped, missing file still sends lost summary mail DAG integrity for build_report and the weekly DAG orchestration regressions a read only guard test: collector issues only SELECT statements accidental writes

Never weaken a test to get green. A fix ships with a regression test that failed first.

docs.title: 14. Build plan for agents
docs.text:
One concern per branch (feature/report-...), small PRs, tests with the code, PR opened and then stop. Commit scope reports is not in the allowed list in docs/GITWORKFLOWS.md yet: ask a human to add it to the doc and the commit-msg hook, or use repo meanwhile.

Phase Deliverable Done when 0 read AGENTS.md, the docs listed at the top, the audit DDL and legacy/ for visual hints a written list of real column names and open questions in the PR description 1 config/, context.schema.json, five fixtures, paths.py schema validates all fixtures, unit tests green 2 render.py, bankingreport.sty, templates, main.tex, latexmkrc, report-fixture make ci green, no unrendered tags 3 charts.py, flow.py, figures wired into chapters charts render from fixtures, empty data placeholders work 4 compile.py, reports/Dockerfile, apt-packages.txt, report-pdf, report-docker all fixtures compile in the container within the page budget 5 collect.py read only guard test green, run once against a disposable or approved database with approval 6 severity.py and rule tests every rule has a passing and a failing case 7 Airflow task, mail attachment, compose volume, image change, env vars DAG integrity and mail tests green, one approved real run attached to mail 8 incident kind, weekly DAG, watchdog hook incident PDF appears on a seeded failing fixture run 9 docs sync every item in the checklist below is done

Docs to update in the same PRs: docs/AIRFLOW.md (DAG diagram, task table, volume), docs/DEPLOYMENT.md (TeX image, env vars), docs/TESTING.md (tex tier, new regression rows), docs/CI-CD.md (optional nightly report-pdf job), docs/RUNBOOK.md (how to regenerate and read a report), docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md (symptoms below), docs/GITWORKFLOWS.md (scope), reports/README.md (pointer to this page) and AGENTS.md (link and the rules in section 3).

docs.title: 15. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Fix Undefined control sequence in the log unescaped text, or a macro missing from the style file check the .tex line named in the log, make sure the value went through \VAR{} Missing character or tofu glyphs font lacks a glyph keep status glyphs to words, or add the glyph to the fallback chain File 'bankingreport.sty' not found TEXINPUTS not set run through latexmk with the repo latexmkrc, from reports/ Overfull \hbox in tables long identifier or a message that cannot wrap use the ident or breakable filter, or a narrower column; the tex tier fails on any overfull box Blank figure or empty chart no data for that section expected: the placeholder box shows, check sections_failed Charts use the wrong font fonts not registered confirm fonts/*.ttf exist, matplotlib font cache may need clearing Build works locally, fails in Airflow package missing from the image compare apt-packages.txt, rebuild the image Mail arrives without PDF build failed or file over the size limit check build_report logs and REPORT_MAX_ATTACH_MB, the body names the reason Report says UNKNOWN for a step no audit evidence for it expected by rule 6, investigate the missing audit rows, do not default to ok Times look 5.5 hours off known timezone offset issue see open issue 3 in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, do not patch inside the report PDF differs between runs now() leaked into the body or unsorted data fix determinism, set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH

docs.title: 16. Decisions for a human
docs.text:
These block specific phases. Do not guess; list them in the PR and ask.

  1. TeX inside the Airflow worker image (recommended) against a separate builder service. Needs an image size and build time decision.
  2. Font files: resolved. Inter 4.1 and JetBrains Mono 2.304 are in reports/fonts/ with their OFL licence texts, the style file loads them with fontspec and reports/latexmkrc sets $pdf_mode = 5 (XeLaTeX). The lastpage.sty package is still optional for the same reason as before: without it the footer shows "Page x" instead of "Page x of y".
  3. Recipients and the weekly schedule, and whether incident PDFs go to a wider list.
  4. Retention of PDFs and whether archived reports should also go to a bucket or volume.
  5. Whether the report should include a short "known open issues" appendix read from config/ or only link docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
  6. Any severity downgrade or threshold change from the defaults in section 5 and 6.

docs.title: Rules that must not break
docs.text:
• The report only reads. It never writes to the warehouse, Databricks or audit.*.
  • No row values, PII, secrets or credentials in context, figures, LaTeX, logs or mail.
  • Every value is escaped by default; shell escape stays off.
  • Unknown is never shown as success; a failed report never fails the pipeline.
  • Same context in, same PDF out.
  • Thresholds and severities change only with human approval.
  • The mail path is the existing one; attachments extend it, they do not replace it.

docs.title: Definition of done
docs.text:
• make ci green, including report-fixture; make report-pdf green where TeX exists
  • every new test is marked and actually runs under its make target
  • all five fixtures render and compile within the page budget
  • schema, fixtures and templates agree on schema_version
  • tasks.bat has the same targets as the Makefile
  • new environment variables are in both example env files
  • DAG integrity and mail tests cover the new task and attachment
  • one approved real run produced a PDF in the mail, with the verdict matching audit.pipeline_runs.status
  • docs listed in section 14 updated in the same PRs
  • restricted actions were approved and the approval is quoted in the PR

docs.title: Runbook — Banking-Delta-Lakehouse
docs.text: Day-to-day operations: run it, watch it, recover it. Diagram colour legend: docs/PIPELINE.md (red = failure paths, green = healthy, slate = audit, violet = actions).

docs.title: How a run happens
docs.text:
Path Trigger Notes Scheduled Airflow banking_delta_daily, 0 2 * * * Asia/Kolkata created paused — un-pause deliberately Manual (Airflow) airflow dags trigger banking_delta_daily --conf '{"publish_full": true}' for a full republish Manual (host) python main.py or make daily same 10 gated steps (preflight first), stops at first failure

max_active_runs=1: a trigger fired while a run is active waits and then runs the whole pipeline again — it does not run concurrently.

docs.title: Daily health check
docs.text:
# Airflow side
DC="docker compose -f airflow/docker-compose.yml --env-file airflow/.env.airflow"
$DC exec airflow-scheduler airflow dags list-runs -o table
$DC exec airflow-scheduler \
  airflow tasks states-for-dag-run banking_delta_daily "<run_id>"

# Audit side (source of truth for the summary mail)
psql -c "SELECT status, total_tables, successful_tables, failed_tables, started_at, ended_at
         FROM audit.pipeline_runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 5;"
psql -c "SELECT layer, script_name, status, violation_count, run_at
         FROM audit.dq_run ORDER BY run_at DESC LIMIT 10;"

Watchdog mail (every 3 h, silent when healthy):

Subject marker Meaning Action [MISSED] no successful run in WATCHDOG_MAX_AGE_HOURS (30) investigate last runs below; incident PDF attached [STUCK] a run is RUNNING/PARTIAL older than WATCHDOG_STUCK_HOURS (5) see "Recovery"; incident PDF attached [WATCHDOG-ERROR] warehouse unreachable from the watchdog check DB/network first; incident PDF attached

docs.text:
flowchart TB

Rules while triaging: - Never relax a DQ threshold to make a layer pass — investigate the data or ask (AGENTS.md). - Read statuses, counts and names — not row values (docs/AUDIT.md). - The summary banner can say [FAILED] on a green run (known Airflow-context bug, docs/AIRFLOW.md) — cross-check audit.pipeline_runs.status before believing it.

docs.title: Running one layer (debugging)
docs.text:
python main.py --list                        # the 10 step names
python main.py --only staging-load           # one step
python scripts/run_jobs.py --sources mongo   # one extract
python scripts/run_staging_tests.py --list   # what a DQ runner would do
python scripts/run_staging_tests.py --only 03 -v

make staging && make dq-staging              # via Make
make analytics && make dq-analytics
make marts && make dq-marts
make publish

Pipeline targets hit the environment .env points at — confirm it is the right one first. These actions need approval for non-dev environments (AGENTS.md).

docs.title: First incremental run of a new table
docs.text:
python scripts/seed_watermarks.py --dry-run   # show what would be seeded
python scripts/seed_watermarks.py             # MAX at source -> audit.extract_watermarks

Skip this and the first run re-lands the whole table as an append. MySQL is deliberately absent (full loads). Never rewind a watermark unless --force + a human decision; watermarks advance only inside the load transaction.

docs.title: Republishing marts
docs.text:
python src/jobs/publish_marts.py --tables mart_support_performance   # one mart
python src/jobs/publish_marts.py --full                             # everything, ignores watermarks
python src/jobs/publish_marts.py --lookback 3                       # re-read last 3 months
# or trigger the DAG with the publish_full param

Why: with PUBLISH_LOOKBACK_MONTHS=0 (default) late/edited rows in older months are not republished (caused the mart_support_performance 193-row gap). Durable fix — non-zero lookback and/or periodic --full — is an open item, not applied.

docs.title: Reading and regenerating the report
docs.text:
The PDF report is built from the audit schema, so it can be rebuilt at any time.

make report-fixture                 # render every fixture, no TeX, no database
make report-pdf                     # compile every fixture to PDF (needs latexmk)
make report-tex                     # compile every fixture and check log and page budget
make report-docker                  # compile inside the TeX image (needs docker)
make report                         # daily report for the warehouse in .env
make report-incident RUN=<run id>   # incident report for one run
make report-weekly                  # weekly digest

The PDFs land in reports/output/runs/<run key>/, with a latest copy per kind in reports/output/. The context the report was built from sits next to it as context.json, and the redacted compile log is in reports/build/report.log for the daily build, incident.log or weekly.log for the others. Design and rule reference: docs/REPORTING.md.

Regenerating a specific run's report (e.g. for an incident review):

make report-incident RUN=scheduled__2026-10-20T20:30:00+00:00

This produces incident.pdf for that run and places it in reports/output/runs/<run key>/.

Weekly digest — runs Monday 08:00 IST via banking_report_weekly DAG; can be regenerated manually:

make report-weekly

Produces weekly.pdf with trends, volumes, DQ and freshness over the last 14 runs.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text:
Situation What to do Killed worker, table_runs stuck RUNNING finalize_audit (Airflow all_done task, or python -m banking_airflow.finalize_audit) reaps then recomputes; fail_stale_runs(6h) runs at the start of the next job Duplicate trigger queued by max_active_runs=1 expected — it runs after the current one finishes; unqueue it from the UI only if you really mean to skip it Watermark conflict (WatermarkConflict) another run advanced the watermark first; let the retry re-read the window — never hand-edit the watermark Partial load (PARTIAL) find failed table_runs, fix, re-run that layer's load step; raw/watermarks are untouched on failure Need the pipeline from scratch on a disposable DB re-apply sql/scripts in order (make sql-smoke pattern) and seed watermarks

Mail path check (read-only, safe):

docker compose -f airflow/docker-compose.yml --env-file airflow/.env.airflow \
  exec airflow-worker python -m banking_airflow.notify --test

docs.title: Escalation
docs.text: Anything that touches the real warehouse, Databricks, merges to main, timezone/watermark behaviour changes, or DQ thresholds: ask a human first (AGENTS.md). Open known issues are listed in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

docs.title: Testing — Banking-Delta-Lakehouse
docs.text:
Two kinds of tests live here:

  1. SQL data-quality suites (tests/data-quality/) — test the data against a populated warehouse. See docs/DATA-QUALITY.md.
  2. Python tests (tests/, airflow/tests/) — test the code, hermetically. This document.

Rules: never weaken a test to get green (AGENTS.md).

docs.title: Test tiers
docs.text:
Tier Marker Make target Needs Agent may run Lint / format — lint, format ruff yes SQL lint — sql-lint sqlfluff yes Unit unit unit, cov nothing external yes Smoke smoke smoke, test nothing external yes Spark smoke spark spark-smoke Java 8/11/17/21 ask first SQL smoke — sql-smoke disposable PG + ALLOW_SQL_SMOKE=1 ask first Integration integration integration disposable PG + ALLOW_SQL_SMOKE=1 ask first Live smoke live smoke-live real configured env (read-only) ask first DQ gate (data) — dq-*, dq populated warehouse ask first Report TeX tex report-tex, report-pdf, report-docker TeX Live or Docker yes Report TeX CI tex report-tex Docker image (no host TeX) CI only Gate — ci = lint + sql-lint + unit + smoke + report-fixture — yes

Unit test: one function/class in isolation; collaborators faked; deterministic; no I/O except tmp_path. Smoke test: fast "is it wired up?" checks — every module imports, every CLI answers --help/--list, repo/SQL/env contracts hold. Not logic tests. Integration test: real disposable PostgreSQL, real stored procedures, synthetic rows.

Markers are registered in pyproject.toml ([tool.pytest.ini_options] markers); unmarked tests are not selected by make unit / make smoke and silently never run. Mark every test (@pytest.mark.unit) or set pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit at module top.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
tests/
├── conftest.py            # fake_env (deterministic config), no_network (autouse)
├── smoke/                 # marker: smoke
│   ├── test_imports.py    # every src/scripts/dashboard-lib module imports
│   ├── test_cli_contracts.py   # main.py --list, run_jobs --help, ...
│   ├── test_repo_contract.py   # required files, markers, hermetic ci, untracked .env
│   ├── test_sql_contract.py    # master loads, unique numbering, DQ suite contract
│   └── test_env_contract.py    # every require()d var is in .env.example
├── unit/                  # one test module per source module, all collaborators faked
├── integration/           # disposable PG only
└── data-quality/          # SQL DQ suites — do not move (docs/DATA-QUALITY.md)
airflow/tests/             # Airflow wiring: DAG integrity, commands, summary, redaction

testpaths = ["tests", "airflow/tests"]. Mirror the source path in test names (src/utils/audit.py → tests/unit/utils/test_audit.py); files test_<module>.py, tests test_<behaviour>_<condition>_<expected>.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
1. Arrange / Act / Assert, one behaviour per test; pytest.mark.parametrize for case tables.
  2. Hermetic by default — tests/conftest.py blocks socket.socket.connect for unit/smoke tests. Fake drivers (pymysql, pymongo, psycopg2, databricks.sql) with monkeypatch; never import real connections at module scope.
  3. Config via fake_env / monkeypatch.setenv, never by editing .env (src/utils/config.py is the only reader and uses override=False).
  4. Filesystem via tmp_path; no writes to .spark/, logs/ or the repo root.
  5. Time: timezone-aware UTC only (datetime.now(timezone.utc)); inject or freeze time; no sleep.
  6. Money: Decimal("123.45") / NUMERIC(18,2); never float.
  7. No row values or secrets in assertions or logs — counts, names, statuses only.
  8. Windows-safe: pathlib, sys.executable, encoding="utf-8" on every open/read_text, no fcntl/signal.setitimer (see airflow/tests/conftest.py stubs). The repo has been bitten by cp1252 consoles.
  9. Fast: one unit test < 100 ms; unit tier < 1 min; smoke tier < 1 min.
  10. Deterministic and order-independent.

docs.title: Inner loop
docs.text:
uv run pytest tests/smoke/test_imports.py -q    # one file
uv run pytest -m unit -k redact -x              # keyword, stop on first failure
pwsh scripts/run_tests.ps1                      # every test file + all 4 DQ suites, report at the end
make format                                      # auto-fix style
make ci                                          # lint + sql-lint + unit + smoke

scripts/run_tests.ps1 runs each pytest file on its own, then the raw/staging/analytics/marts DQ runners, and prints a per-file report with totals (saved to logs/test-report-<stamp>.txt, exit 1 on any failure). -SkipDq drops the DQ suites, -Filter <text> picks files, -Marker all runs every marker (spark, tex, ...) instead of the default unit or smoke.

Restricted (ask first): make spark-smoke, ALLOW_SQL_SMOKE=1 make sql-smoke integration (disposable PG only), make smoke-live.

docs.title: Definition of done
docs.text:
• make ci green locally; make cov if covered code changed (never lower fail_under).
  • New behaviour has a test; a fix ships with a regression test that failed before it.
  • Extra tiers the change requires were run, or listed as "not run, needs approval".
  • Every new test has a marker and actually runs under make unit / make smoke.

docs.title: Do a small group of customers drive most transaction value?
docs.text:
Business question: Head of Retail Banking / CRM lead would ask this to decide where retention and cross-sell budget goes.

Data used: marts.mart_customer_360 (grain: one row per customer)

Finding: Among customers with transaction activity, the top 10% by transaction value account for 22.55% of total transaction value (2,727,440,949.25 of 12,096,774,249.05).

Segment view: By income band, Upper-Mid (36.12%) and High (32.88%) hold 69.00% of value from 32,786 of 47,640 active customers, but average value is flat at 250,806.60-255,284.46 across all five bands. So what: rank on value, not income - an income-tier campaign would over-serve low-value customers in high bands. Query: docs/insights/queries/customer_segments.sql.

So what: Prioritise retention, fee-waiver and cross-sell offers for the top decile, and run a reactivation journey for the 12,361 customers with no transaction activity.

Reproduce: docs/insights/queries/customer_concentration.sql with psql -U postgres -d banking_delta -f docs/insights/queries/customer_concentration.sql

docs.title: How late is the loan book paying?
docs.text:
Business question: Chief Risk Officer / Head of Collections would ask this to size provisioning and collection capacity.

Data used: marts.mart_loan_portfolio (grain: one row per loan type x status x loan amount band x term band x disbursement year)

Finding: 12.01% of 600,005 loan payments are late (72,038), against a total loan book of 9,214,897,690.78 spread evenly across six loan types (16.49-16.80% each).

Segment view: Late rates stay flat by loan size (11.88% under 1L, 12.04% for 1-5L) and by type (11.85% Business Loan to 12.19% Auto Loan). So what: there is no size or product segment to prioritize; reminders and collections should cover the whole book. Query: docs/insights/queries/loan_segments.sql.

So what: Add automated payment reminders and a 30-day collections queue for late payers; product mix is already diversified, so collections, not rebalancing, is the lever.

Reproduce: docs/insights/queries/loan_late_payment.sql with psql -U postgres -d banking_delta -f docs/insights/queries/loan_late_payment.sql

docs.title: How much fraud is in card spend?
docs.text:
Business question: Fraud Operations lead would ask this to set detection thresholds and investigator staffing.

Data used: marts.mart_card_fraud (grain: one row per month x card type x card category x card tier x merchant category)

Finding: Fraud accounts for 0.499% of 3,005,000 card transactions (15,006 transactions, 28,608,185.59), with rates between 0.497% and 0.524% across merchant categories.

Segment view: Fraud rate is 0.479% for Platinum and 0.507% for Classic, and Debit cards (tier N/A) carry 15,673,144.60 of the fraud amount. So what: tier-specific blocking would miss most of the exposure; keep velocity and amount rules on every tier and watch Debit first. Query: docs/insights/queries/card_fraud_segments.sql.

So what: Shift fraud controls to velocity and amount thresholds rather than merchant-category blocking, and size the investigator queue to ~15,000 alerts per period.

Reproduce: docs/insights/queries/card_fraud.sql with psql -U postgres -d banking_delta -f docs/insights/queries/card_fraud.sql

docs.title: Is transaction value concentrated in a few channels?
docs.text:
Business question: Head of Digital Channels / payments lead would ask this to guide channel investment and cost negotiation.

Data used: marts.mart_monthly_transactions (grain: one row per month x transaction type x channel x merchant category x direction x region)

Finding: Total transaction value is 12,096,774,249.05 across 103 months, split almost evenly across six channels (16.62% to 16.70% each).

Segment view: By region, value runs from North 26.76% to East 9.88% (2.7x), while transaction types split 9.97-24.96%. So what: plan capacity and pricing by region; the flat channel mix is not a reason to push traffic between channels for share. Query: docs/insights/queries/transaction_segments.sql.

So what: Negotiate per-channel processing costs and migrate low-value traffic to cheaper channels without risking share, since no single channel dominates.

Reproduce: docs/insights/queries/transaction_channels.sql with psql -U postgres -d banking_delta -f docs/insights/queries/transaction_channels.sql

docs.title: Are branches evenly loaded?
docs.text:
Business question: Head of Branch Network / COO would ask this to rebalance staffing and service levels.

Data used: marts.mart_branch_performance (grain: one row per branch)

Finding: Across 151 branches, accounts per employee ranges from 27.55 to 211.33 (average 58.27) and branch late-payment rates range from 10.60% to 13.77%.

Segment view: Regionally, West branches average 65.38 accounts per employee against North 53.11, while late-payment rates stay within 11.96-12.14%. So what: move staff toward West and Central offices; a 0.18pp regional late-rate spread does not justify separate collections playbooks. Query: docs/insights/queries/branch_segments.sql.

So what: Rebalance staff and automate servicing in high-load branches, and replicate collection practices from branches at the low end of the late-payment range.

Reproduce: docs/insights/queries/branch_workload.sql with psql -U postgres -d banking_delta -f docs/insights/queries/branch_workload.sql

docs.title: Is customer support meeting its SLA?
docs.text:
Business question: Head of Customer Service would ask this to prioritise issue types and service recovery.

Data used: marts.mart_support_performance (grain: one row per month opened x issue type x status x customer state x income band)

Finding: Of 25,300 support tickets, 79.67% (20,156) are resolved, average satisfaction is 3.00/5, and 39.95% (10,108) scored 2 or below.

Segment view: Resolution ranges from 78.61% (Account Statement) to 81.15% (Net Banking Issue), satisfaction stays flat at 2.97-3.04 across issue types, and the Low income band resolves worst (78.36%). So what: fix statement, KYC and loan-query workflows first, but treat low satisfaction as systemic rather than issue-specific. Query: docs/insights/queries/support_segments.sql.

So what: Launch service recovery for the 10,108 low-satisfaction tickets and root-cause the "Account Statement" issue type, which has the lowest resolution rate at 78.61%.

Reproduce: docs/insights/queries/support_sla.sql with psql -U postgres -d banking_delta -f docs/insights/queries/support_sla.sql
